properties.thesis: School-zone demand should support resale, but the room may price in the upside before you own it.
properties.main_risk: Family buyers push the auction beyond the renovation margin.
properties.best_strategy: Use agent comps, set a disciplined cap, and only renovate presentation items.
properties.bad_strategy: Keep bidding because Northbank feels safe.
properties.notes: School-zone cottage with dated interiors and a deep back yard.

properties.thesis: Cheap because it presents badly, but the large block gives the deal a second way to work.
properties.main_risk: A structural defect turns the cheap entry into an expensive rescue.
properties.best_strategy: Inspect deeply, cap the bid hard, and repair only if the defect is confirmed.
properties.bad_strategy: Overbid because the guide looks low.
properties.notes: Large block, poor presentation, and serious upside if defects stay manageable.

properties.thesis: The house looks easy, but the safety premium leaves little room after fees.
properties.main_risk: You pay full retail for a property with limited upside.
properties.best_strategy: Buy only below fair value and avoid cosmetic spending that buyers already expect.
properties.bad_strategy: Mistake low defect risk for a guaranteed profit.
properties.notes: Move-in ready family home with less upside but fewer nasty surprises.

properties.thesis: Cheap entry and low holding costs help, but the repair bill decides the deal.
properties.main_risk: Defects consume the whole discount before resale demand arrives.
properties.best_strategy: Buy only with a repair allowance and sell quickly if the defect is real.
properties.bad_strategy: Treat renovation potential as profit before pricing the damage.
properties.notes: Entry-level renovator with cheap holding costs and weak buyer emotion.

properties.thesis: High appeal attracts bidders, but the price already captures most of the good news.
properties.main_risk: Premium holding costs punish a slow resale.
properties.best_strategy: Only bid if the room stays cool and sell with a conservative reserve.
properties.bad_strategy: Pay extra because the house feels finished.
properties.notes: High appeal, high price, and limited room for a quick flip margin.

properties.thesis: Patchy auction demand and improving transport create a stronger rental yield than resale margin.
properties.main_risk: A forced early sale leaves little profit after fees.
properties.best_strategy: Buy below reserve pressure, place a tenant, and let the rent support the next deposit.
properties.bad_strategy: Ignore it because the room is not excited.
properties.notes: Industrial-edge suburb with improving transport links and patchy demand.

properties.thesis: A compact home near transport offers dependable rent without tying up a premium-sized deposit.
properties.main_risk: Limited land and only two bedrooms cap resale emotion.
properties.best_strategy: Protect the yield, lease quickly, and resist a prestige renovation.
properties.bad_strategy: Spend like it is a large family flip.
properties.notes: Compact brick home near the tram terminus with strong tenant enquiry.

properties.thesis: The broad block and ugly interior advertise upside to every experienced renovator in the room.
properties.main_risk: Competitive bidders pay today for improvements that still cost money tomorrow.
properties.best_strategy: Inspect first and make the room leave you a real works budget.
properties.bad_strategy: Count the full renovated value before paying for the renovation.
properties.notes: Original seventies interior on a wide block with a questionable rear extension.

properties.thesis: A plain court location suppresses auction theatre while the extra bathroom supports tenants and resale.
properties.main_risk: Soft local demand makes a fast resale uncertain.
properties.best_strategy: Buy the numbers, place a tenant, and wait for a stronger exit market.
properties.bad_strategy: Ignore it because nobody else looks excited.
properties.notes: Unfashionable but practical home with an unusually useful second bathroom.

properties.thesis: The low quote guarantees a crowd, but the vendor expects Northbank money despite the defects.
properties.main_risk: The reserve and repair bill consume the apparent guide-price discount.
properties.best_strategy: Use full diligence and treat the guide as advertising, not valuation.
properties.bad_strategy: Anchor your plan to the first number on the brochure.
properties.notes: Crowd-pulling Northbank address with visible cracking and an ambitious vendor.

properties.thesis: School demand makes the exit reliable, but families will fight for the same certainty at purchase.
properties.main_risk: A beautiful house creates the confidence to abandon your own limit.
properties.best_strategy: Bid only while a clean margin survives and avoid unnecessary upgrades.
properties.bad_strategy: Treat strong resale demand as permission to pay any price.
properties.notes: Turn-key school-zone home designed to make bidders feel safe.

properties.thesis: The house is almost irrelevant; patient capital is buying a scarce industrial-edge block.
properties.main_risk: Developer competition appears suddenly once the land value is recognised.
properties.best_strategy: Price the land, inspect the dwelling, and do not beautify a future site.
properties.bad_strategy: Renovate the house while ignoring what makes the deal valuable.
properties.notes: A neglected cottage on one of Westport's largest remaining residential blocks.

upgrades.description: Cheap presentation lift. Reliable, but not a miracle.

upgrades.description: Family buyers notice it fast. Works best in high-demand suburbs.

upgrades.name: Bathroom Upgrade
upgrades.description: Solid value boost with moderate cost.

upgrades.name: Landscaping
upgrades.description: Raises auction energy more than the valuation spreadsheet admits.

upgrades.name: Structural Repair
upgrades.description: Expensive risk control. Often necessary, rarely exciting.

upgrades.name: Staging
upgrades.description: Short-lived sale boost for emotional bidding.

market_events.title: Week 1 Market News
items: Northbank family homes are hot this week. Buyer demand rises sharply.
Renovation grants are being discussed, lifting fixer-upper interest.
Banks keep rates steady, so borrowing capacity holds.
market_events.strategy_effect: Hot family demand rewards clean exits, but auction rooms will stretch faster than spreadsheets.

market_events.title: Week 2 Market News
items: Interest rate fears trim buyer budgets across the board.
Eastvale school ranking improves, supporting family demand.
Developers are cautious unless the land component is strong.
market_events.strategy_effect: Higher borrowing stress favours cheaper entries, larger buffers, and walking away early.

market_events.title: Week 3 Market News
items: Transport upgrade rumours lift Westport buyer interest.
Cosmetic renovations are performing well at auction.
Premium homes are taking longer to sell.
market_events.strategy_effect: Cosmetic improvements can work, but premium homes need sharper purchase discipline.

market_events.title: Week 4 Market News
items: Rental vacancy falls in Westport and Southmere, lifting advertised rents.
Northbank clearance rates remain high despite more cautious lenders.
Building inspectors report delays on structural assessments.
market_events.strategy_effect: Yield assets can support the next purchase while defect-heavy projects need a wider time buffer.

market_events.title: Week 5 Market News
items: A surprise rate cut restores borrowing power across the city.
Ridgefield large blocks attract renewed developer interest.
Eastvale listings remain scarce ahead of school enrolments.
market_events.strategy_effect: Cheaper finance expands your options, but it also puts more paddles into every quality auction.

market_events.title: Week 6 Market News
items: Auction volumes surge, giving disciplined buyers more alternatives.
Premium-home clearance rates soften in Northbank and Eastvale.
Affordable rentals continue to lease within days.
market_events.strategy_effect: A crowded schedule rewards selectivity: premium vendors may blink while affordable holds stay competitive.
